BGE Ladder Component.
How it works: 
Go to a ladder component and hold the e-key to climb up, down or sideways.
Every ladder component has a property called ladder and the PlayerBox searches for this property
with a near-sensor.
Every time you near to an object that contains the ladder property you get a gameinfo E-Key on the screen so you know that you can climb.
P-Key.................Starts the Game Engine
W-Key.................Move forwards
S-Key.................Move backwards
D-Key.................Move to the right
A-Key.................Move to the left
Hold Spacebar.........Player moves faster
Q-Key.................Jump
F-Key.................Changed the daytime forward
B-Key.................Changed the daytime backward
E-Key.................Climb up

title: T-Splines Rhino School Building 3d model Free 3D print model
formats: 3DM
formats_detail: [{"format": "3DM", "full_name": "Rhinoceros 3D", "file_size": "470 MB", "file_count": 1, "version": "", "renderer": null}]
total_file_size: 3DM:470 MB
description_text:
This building was modeled in Rhino using the T-splines and grasshopper plugins. It was designed for my Masters of Architecture Studio at Pratt Institute in the spring of 2015.
I have 3D printed this model and it comes out nicely on the higher resolution powder printers (Pictures/Renderings below) This model is designed with some hollow splines so as to use less material (cheaper to print) and has void holes in the back of the model in order to get the powder out after printed. It is chopped at the bottom so as to stand upright, and has an elevator core running up the back of the model, also makes the model less fragile. 
This model looks awesome on a desk or on a shelf. This model is already at scale (about 7-8 inches tall), and can be scaled up if you would like. I would not recommend scaling it down as some of the thinner splines can get too small and might break when excavating the print. 
This model took me around 90 hours to build, you will see the density of the model when you open the file (large file size), but the file still navigates well.  This model can also be imported into Maya, 3DS MAX, Revit, etc. ENJOY!

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Is it a Japanese Tea house? Is it in the Oriental Far East? If you answered yes to either of those questions, I'm sorry to say you are incorrect. But if you said it was in Paulwall then you are indeed correct! Here is a small bungalow house just west of the downtown metro area. It is actually a typical small rectangular bungalow if you think about it. The sharp peaks and long planks were inspired by the Japanese homes made of wood and rice paper. Thank goodness none of this house was made of paper! the porch and chimneys are stuccoed where as the walls are shingle style. Don't stop out here. Come on inside to see striking millwork about the interior. There are built-ins. The dining room also has some fine millwork of its own including a built-in cabinet. You aso get a private porch off the dining room beleive it or not. The kitchen is decked out with retro appliances. in back you get two bedrooms, a bathroom and a sleeping porch, or in other words, a third bedroom if you think about it. Those areas are less intricate. There are a number of other bungalows in the area a lot like this one but minus all the oriental pattern details this one offers. I hope you like this little house and please rate :)

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 13 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 So you are likely already familiar with the fact that Paulwall has a lot of old homes. This one happened to be renovated from its original 4 bedroom, 1 bathroom version to 3 bedrooms and 2.5 bathrooms. This is not a Sears Home, though, it is a Gordon Van Tine Home. It is similar to a foursquare house though people may not call it that. Like any kit home, you'd walk into a great big living room, beyond, a dining room, then a kitchen in the far back corner. Basement stairs would be below the main stair. The laundry room used to be the pantry. The furnace is in the basement, then rides a chase up through the house in the form of a chimney. The building itself, built in the 20's is a relic of mail-order homes mass produced for the growth of cities. Sit on its grand porch, the signature item, or in the singanature bay window upstairs. Either way, you might like to live in this home. It is an 8-minute bus ride to downtown Paulwall or in 10 minute walking proximity to the Paulwall College main campus. This is also near a busy shopping center. The house is in a neighborhood full of other beautifully preserved old homes with tree-lined streets. Enjoy and please rate :)

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Paulwall has an old granite clad city hall. It is known commonly as the community auditorium. Yes, there is a theatre-like auditorium in the rear with a stage, curtains, and skytower. The house has a seating capacity of 500, though the area is currently unaccessable at this time. There is a large seating balcony. though you can't go in, you can see where it exisits on the exterior walls. Paulwall is known well for its ambience in eclectic classical architecture in which you will find in abundance throughout this building. The city lot this building sits on is too small for the complete parking capacity so a seperate lot across the street suffices for it, not modeled here. Half of Paulwall's downtown is just parking lots. Okay, so besides the house in the back, the city offices are in the wings in front. The mayor's office is on the 3rd floor. The smaller building to the right used to be the city library but since they moved, it became offices for the departments of health and education. Ignore the geo-location. Thanks to the contributors for the greenery and google for the flag and dumpsters. everything else was by me. No city is complete without a city hall building. Include in your city backdrop, pefect for downtown. I hope you enjoy one of Paulwall's finest buildings and please rate. IGNORE the geo-location, it isn't real. If you like architecture and want to see more, please check out my community page on Facebook shown by the link given to you below :)

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Here is a victorian shell from one in BmrCT's collection, thanks to BmrCT. I liked the house so much that I could invision its floor plan even though it was a hollow shell so I gave it a floor plan. What you have are stairs as soon as you walk into the entry. To the left is adining room, to the right is the living room with a window seat. In the back you have the kitchen. The kitchen was designed so you can put a round breakfast table in the center. Off to the side of that is a powder room with a bifold pantry directly next to it. In the far back are the basement stairs and the servant's stairway, you know, like in those old houses. The basement stairs are there, not under the main stairs. That is where the coat closet is. Upstairs there are 3 bedrooms and one bathroom. Up where the gothic window is above the front door is a sitting nook. That's the tour. The cosmetic features have been updated and altered some as you can see when comparing it to the original house. Windows have either been added or removed. Both porches were cosmetically redone. There was a lot of cleanup of stray lines about the interior before construction. Another thing, the great chimney in the back once housed an old woodburning stove. That was bricked off and a stainless steelo gas range takes its place. Although I still intend to adjust the cosmetics from time to time, I think it really turned out! Please rate. there is a link to my Facebook page of architecture and homes :)

BUT don't let that discourage you from downloading this authenticlly acurate model. It is a great house with 6 bedrooms, 3.5 bathrooms, and with a uniquely interesting central atrium. I can asure you that the model is structurally correct, the dimensions are accurate, and the coloring is up to par. I admit, I don't have the intricate wall paper patterns but I used a similar color in replacement. The house looks fairly different for it has been remodeled substantially since the murders. I didn't find enough sources to make an accurate today's house but had plenty for the 1974 version. Enjoy it. Oh, yeah, it includes all built-ins (except the bar in sunroom), it remains unfurnished. description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Here is one building of a 6-building housing project. I modeled this tall apartment house after the famous Brewster Wheeler Housing Project in Detroit Michigan Near downtown. I understand this is the year these tall buildings along with some townhouses will be demolished by the city but I liked the designs so I modeled it. This is the tallest building in Paulwall standing at 15 stories in counting! If you are wondering about the first floor, it is sunken into the ground by a few feet. The vestibule has a few steps leading downward. No apartments on the first floor, just the second and so on up. Turn the roof layer off to see the top floor. 8 apartments, a trash room, mechanical room (empty), mail chute, stairs, and an elevator shaft. Each house has 2 small bedrooms, walk-in pantry, one bathroom, and so on. I modeled this old house using whatever photos I could find online as well as watching the videos about it. Diana Ross and the Supremes lived here for a little while. It was the first subsidized house in America for African Americans. Completed in 1952. I hope you enjoy this old house and please rate. Though the actual thing exists in Detroit, you may feel free to put it into your inner city. You can remove the apartments and make it a background object if you like :)

In light of being in the way of something this meaningful, I decided to give you something special! I'm sure a lot of you have heard of and admire the arts of Sir Frank Lloyd Wright. Quite a few have uploaded Frank Lloyd Wrights so I thought, Why not? However, I have not found anyone who's uploaded this particular house. About this house, it was built in 1940, on a steep hillface off of the beautiful Lake Mendota in Wisconsin. The construction was also unusual which consisted of stone counterforts and diagonal ship-lap siding. The home is also unsual because of the low ceilings. The first floor: 6'9Second Floor 7'6. The house was made with its exact dimentions. I used his sections, scaled floor plan, and whatever pictures I've scrounged off the internet (lots). Though the home has changed a little, I made the home as it is seen today by visitors. Take a look, even at the ceilings, fireplace, stone-lined revine, carport, and basement rafters. Upstairs has 3 small bedrooms with built-in beds and one bathroom. A particular acknowledgement would be the famous origami chairs in the living room. Although they were not in the origional plan, they were added later, sitting there today. They were modeled by my good friend, Jeff Myers (JATdesigns) however, everything else was crafted by me. Enjoy this model. The layers will make it easy for you. I hope you have as much fun looking through it as I had in making it. I have a Facebook Page now :)

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Located just north of Paulwall's downtown district, there are a number of beautifully preserved victorian houses. Few, however, remain single family homes for some were broken into apartments, some are offices for companies who bought them, and a few are abandoned. But each are unique not only to each other but to the other houses in the community. These are the houses that get photographed. For example, this one here with its intricate brick work, signiture turret, pointed arch in front, is a great example of a guilded age mansion. They do not make them like this anymore which is why people like to visit Paulwall, to see what is left of its eclectic architecture. See its fancy chimnies or the widow's walk on the roof. You even see the trapdoor hatch! Forgive this shell model for it does not yet have an interior (but will have one soon). Though, in the mean time, lots of details to see and to enjoy. You can even use it as a backdrop object for your urban neighborhood scene! Welcome to the Ransom Gillis House! Although the origin is in Brush Park, Detroit, Paulwall proudly holds a replica of it. Enjoy and please rate. I have a page on Facebook set up for architecture and Sketchup enthusiasts so check out my link below if you wish :)

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 It is a 40's tract house. These houses were very common in the United States in cities used mainly by the working class and incoming veterans. In this time period, there was a skyrocket in the demand for housing so many houses were needed in a short time. Tract homes were very cookie cutter so you would step out onto your porch to see a copy of your house across the street. However, the homes weren't all the same. They varied by neighborhood and time period. It was common that tract homes had 2 bedrooms but this model actually has 4. It also has 2 full bathrooms (another rare comfort)! There is a basement. I am not a fan of tract-style kitchens so I designed the kitchen. It is designed for the tabe to be right there in the kitchen. There is a wroght iron column in front along with a living room picture window. There is good clost space here. The chimney is actually the furnace vent trailing all the way to the basement. These houses most commonly found near factories or jumbled around downtown. Either way, I hope you enjoy this tract house. Please rate. For more houses and architecture, don't forget to check out my Facebook page given at the link below.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Here is a classy additon to my collection. This southern colonial stately looking house would be a fine addition to your southern neighborhood. It has that plantation feeling with its large front colonade and massive chimneys. All around you will find classic finishes to give it a good appeal. Expensive looking too. Come on in to a tall foyer. Here, this house has a living room (or den) in front with a large family room behind (both have fire places). On your left, there is a formal dining room. Beyond are the kitchen and breakfast room. Kitchen pantry is behind the refridgerator. One chimney has the two fire places, the other chimney is the mechanical rool. This house has 3 bedrooms and 2.5 bathrooms. There is a powder room off the entryway. Looking for the coat closet? It is in that little hall betwwen laundry room and garage. You get a deluxe master suite with all the fixin's. It actually takes up the entire right wing of the house! Out back is a massive wooden deck with cherry stain. A greenhouse/ sunroom is around the side I hope this house gives you a feeling of the south. I could swear I heard some bluegrass somewhere. Anyway, enjoy this classic colonial house and please rate :)

Historically a part of Lancashire, Ancoats became one of the cradles of the Industrial Revolution, and has been called the world's first industrial suburb. The area suffered accelerating economic decline from the 1930s and depopulation in the years after the Second World War, particularly during the slum clearances of the 1960s.
Since the 1990s Ancoats' industrial heritage has been recognised and this, along with its proximity to the city centre, has led to investment and the development of substantial regeneration plans.

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 (Modified version)   ==============   Naqsh-e Jahan Square (Persian: میدان نقش جهان‎ Maidān-e Naqsh-e Jahān; trans: Image of the World Square), known as Imam Square (میدان امام), formerly known as Shah Square (میدان شاه), is a square situated at the center of Isfahan city, Iran. Constructed between 1598 and 1629, it is now an important historical site, and one of UNESCO's World Heritage Sites. It is 160 meters wide by 508 meters long[1] (an area of 89,600 m2). The square is surrounded by buildings from the Safavid era. The Shah Mosque is situated on the south side of this square. On the west side is the Ali Qapu Palace. Sheikh Lotf Allah Mosque is situated on the eastern side of this square and the northern side opens into the Isfahan Grand Bazaar. Today, Namaaz-e Jom'eh (the Muslim Friday prayer) is held in the Shah Mosque.

The professor had suffered from a cerebral hemorrhage and died, never returning to the train station where Hachikō was waiting. Every day for the next nine years the golden brown Akita waited at Shibuya station.------------Hachikō was given away after his master's death, but he routinely escaped, returning again and again to his old home. Eventually, Hachikō apparently realized that Professor Ueno no longer lived at the house. So he went to look for his master at the train station where he had accompanied him so many times before. Each day, Hachikō waited for the return of his owner.------------The permanent fixture at the train station that was Hachikō attracted the attention of other commuters. Many of the people who frequented the Shibuya train station had seen Hachikō and Professor Ueno together each day. They brought Hachikō treats and food to nourish him during his wait.------------  This continued for nine years with Hachikō appearing precisely when the train was due at the station.

description_text:
This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 7 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 I did this diamond Logo to pay homage to the 4th Doctor's Doctor Who Logo, I just updated it for my own purpose but I did not like the idea of the diamond being blank on the other side, so for a bit of fun I put Matt Smiths name there and I wanted my logo to be the same or near to it, the same color as the TARDIS.
I used 3D Text for the lettering, if you can imagine the logo as part of the new Doctor Who title sequence, I hope you can see the potential this logo could have with it spinning around at a good speed, so people can see the logo change from saying Doctor Who To Matt Smith.  Please be gentle with your comments and your rating.  I'm still learning with GoogleSketchUp 7.

description_text:
The Museo Soumaya is a private museum in Mexico City. It has over 66,000 works from 30 centuries of art including sculptures from Pre-Hispanic Mesoamerica, 19th- and 20th-century Mexican art and an extensive repertoire of works by European old masters and masters of modern western art such as Auguste Rodin, Salvador Dalí, Bartolomé Esteban Murillo and Tintoretto. It is considered one of the most complete collections of its kind.
The building is considered Postmodern, it was designed by Mexican architect Fernando Romero, engineered with Ove Arup and Frank Gehry, and finished in 2011.

description_text:
This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 The Freedom Monument (Latvian: Brīvības piemineklis) is a memorial located in Riga, Latvia honoring soldiers killed during the Latvian War of Independence (1918–1920). It is considered an important symbol of the freedom, independence, and sovereignty of Latvia.[1]  Unveiled in 1935, the 42-metre (138 ft) high monument of granite, travertine, and copper  often serves as the focal point of public gatherings and official ceremonies in Riga. (wikipedia.org)
The sculptures and bas-reliefs of the monument, arranged in thirteen groups, depict Latvian culture and history. The core of the monument is composed of tetragonal shapes on top of each other, decreasing in size towards the top, completed by a 19-metre (62 ft) high travertine column bearing the copper figure of Liberty lifting three gilded stars. The concept for the monument first emerged in the early 1920s when the Latvian Prime Minister, Zigfrīds Anna Meierovics, ordered rules to be drawn up for a contest for designs of a memorial column. After several contests the monument was finally built at the beginning of the 1930s according to the scheme Shine like a star! submitted by Latvian sculptor Kārlis Zāle. Construction works were financed by private donations.

The earliest parols were traditionally made from simple materials like bamboo sticks, Japanese rice paper (known as papel de Hapon) or crepe paper, and a candle or coconut oil-lamp for illumination; although the present day parol can take many different shapes and forms.  The most basic parol can be easily constructed with just ten bamboo sticks, paper, and glue. These lanterns represent the Star of Bethlehem that guided the Magi, also known as the Three Wise Men or Three Kings (Tatlong Hari in Tagalog).
Puto Bumbong, Traditionally made from a special variety of heirloom sticky or glutinous rice called Pirurutong which has a distinctly purple color, soaked in salted water and dried overnight and then poured into bumbong or bamboo tubes and then steamed until done or steam rises out of the bamboo tubes. It is served topped with butter or margarine and shredded coconut mixed with sugar.
Puto bumbong is the most sought after delicacies at Christmas time. During the simbang gabi or the Christmas Eve mass, people would line up to their favorite stalls outside the church just to have a taste of this favorite Pinoy delicacies.

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 The red telephone kiosk has become a landmark and has its own national conservation plan. It was born in 1933 after an architectural competition, which was won by architect Georg Fasting from Bergen. The first was set up on Amerikalinjens docked in Oslo. A restored version is currently set up at near-native space (see photo). Only after the war spread this kiosk type to the rest of the country. The location of public telephone boxes always took into account the public safety and should provide easy access to a doctor, midwife, police and fire. They were an obvious staple among apartment blocks in the 60s suburbs, at railway stations and at numerous ferry ports. The public telephone kiosk was primarily a service, and profitability came in second place. The last kiosk was produced in 1995. In total it has been produced about 9,000 copies of this kind, and many are still in use. The design has remained without changes, except for the weight: The first kiosks weighed 800 kg, while later editions weighed less than half. To elaborate on the tower design, it has a geometric cylinder base that houses a large retailer store(Walmart in this case) with an elevator in the middle of the cylinder leading all the way to the roof of the structure. The roof itself resembles that of a true crown. The spire is a DNA double helix strand that has LED lighting and imagery (imaging Target Plaza south 100,000 LED's in a spiral form). The south face of the building also has a double helix pattern running from the 3rd floor to the crown, which would also have animated LED'S. I don't know the market well, but I have faith in Minneapolis. And if you guys show support for this design, who knows? Maybe OPUS will see it and consider it. So let's make this building POPULAR TWIN CITIZENS!!!DISCLAIMER: I DID NOT MAKE THE GLASS TEXTURE! THAT CREDIT GOES TO m b p. So thank him everyone. That person is awesome!

This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 13 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 A simplified model of an RTG lke those used on deep space probes by NASA.  Probes which go further than the orbit of Mars face very low levels of sunlight, making solar panels ineffective as the primary power source.
 An RTG is a decay-based nuclear power source that uses pellets of plutonium-238 to generate heat.  The heat is converted to electricity by a thermoelectric material.
RTGs have been used on the Pioneer and Voyager probes as well as newer probes like the New Horizons probe on its way to Pluto.   They provide decades of reliable power to the spacecraft systems

description_text:
This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 The goal! The main objective of this project is to identify the original attitude of the rock movements, to translate and interpret it into a new architectural language and interior design for a contemporary house in the urban down town of the city. 
How to redefine the meaning of the contemporary house?... Grunge architecture!! Based in a previous knowledge and deep research about the rock culture, is settle a theoretical document that translates the most significant rock values, into architectural shapes and interior design language for the house. Grunge architecture transforms the traditional house into a feelings-machine with new space relations. An architectural element inspired by the punk, the hard rock and the grunge music as well. The cultural and conceptual parameters that have been influenced this kind of music-movements are the research database for this particular project.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This is my train station on my layout.  A little bit of history:  when I went into the service in the 70s, my dad tossed out all my stuff while I was overseas  I guess he was afraid I would come home in a box!.  Fast forward to about 15 years ago.  I was browsing in an antique shop and I found this kit from the 50s.  I bought  it. (My old kit?) A friend of mine said not to build it cause it would decrease the value.  After several models, I built the train station.  It sees a lot of trafic.  I had to add some foundation pieces from Plastruct shapes.  It has been there ever since.  As a bonus, I have included some pictures of my layout.  They were taken with a low-res camera, so they are a  bit fuzzy.  You can see the train starion in its home.  I also included a picture of a bank robbery with the Idaho State Police car which is very valuable and my theatre.  So have fun with this,  The kit does not have stairs, which I added to the model.  This model is 90% components.  The stairs are components, you can edit them to add railings.  This a shell with floors.  Is made up of 3X 3 squares.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 15 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 I have a train station on my layout that is a modular kit.  The kit was made in the 1950s.  It has wall panels and columns that interlock.  After watching a show on cable that had a house I liked, I thought that I would  see if I could make a house of the kit components like that one.  Here it is.  The exterior has 42 columns 24X24 10' high made of extruded concrete.  The wall panels are a sandwich of stamped steel (or aluminum) powder coated white on the outside with auto enamel, a foam core, and drywall taped, textured, and painted on the inside.  Walls are capped with a 2' high parapet.  Front door has a 4' high parapet.  There is 3 bedrooms, 2 1/2 baths, kitchen, dining, and a 2 story livingroom.  The walkout basement is finished.  Highlights: cutout in the Master Bedroom overlooking the living room,  mirrored closet doors, a column in a corner of the master shower, and a wood stove in the Basement.  The Library has a pull-down projector screen.  Finally, a 2-car garage in the house footprint, which measures 51' X 30'.  Exterior walls are components.  You can copy them and make your own house if you want to.  These are only one width of many walls in the kit.  Front door is interactive, I left it open for you.  Close it via Tools>Interact if you want to.  Bob

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This is one of the employees cabins at Sequoia Nat'l Park.  It for the married employees.  There are about 6 of these cabins.  Us single people stay in small cabins in the employees housing area.  This is an exact copy of the floor plan, I just changed the wall materials and roof.  The cabins were built in the 1920s.  They are over-built because there can be as much as 20' of snow in the winter.  One of my jobs was opening the cabin in the spring and closing it in the fall.  The maintainance crew stripped the interior after each season, leaving only what is in there now.  Emplyees who lived there had to scrounge for any extra items they wanted.  Even tho it has been 30 years since I worked there, the cabins may still be there.  Main floor is the living area; there is a sleeping loft above the bath, kitchen and dining area.
